meta.title: Ondra Reflex
meta.description: Self-written reflexes and chain crystallisation with zero model calls (handbook §8.6, P1). The handbook's words: the same tool failing for the same reason three times automatically writes R-auto-<cause>-<tool>, a successful chain of three or more steps across organs crystallises into a skill, and all of it costs no model call. This package does only deterministic rules, sends no model request at all, so its cost is zero, its conclusions are reproducible and its mistakes are traceable. Four judgements. First, attribution is not redefined here: the cause always comes from the failure-attribution service's classification, never from a second taxonomy of our own — the worst outcome of two taxonomies is that one failure is recorded as two different causes in two ledgers, and both then grow contradicting rules. Second, no attribution means no reflex: when attribution is absent the package only counts, and never treats not knowing as the unknown class, otherwise a false cause becomes a long-lived rule. Third, the prescription is not written here either: the one-line hint quotes the attribution service, and this package only decides when a rule should exist. Fourth, crystallisation accepts only successful steps and requires crossing organs, at least two distinct tools, because repeating one tool three times is just the same action done thrice, and freezing that as a skill would teach her to chant. Persistence is a soft requirement: with a store it writes and keeps counting across restarts, without one it stays in memory and says so in its stats. It never feeds the organ host, registers no tools, never touches the dialogue and installs no timers.
